signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.29, holding below its daily SMA200 at 158.50 while anchored above the SMA20 and SMA50 cluster at 156.64/157.79. The nominal policy rate differential of Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% yields a +275bp advantage for USD, reflected in an OIS SOFR-TONA carry spread of +266bp. However, the options market exhibits significant asymmetry: 1M 25d risk reversals print at -2.01, marking a severe put skew that signals elevated institutional hedging against spot downside. Leveraged funds hold net short JPY at -16,809 contracts (CFTC, week ending Sep 29), but that net position ranks in the 96th percentile of its 52-week range (z = +1.83) following a massive 4-week covering surge of +94,488 contracts. BoJ Policy Board member Sato sounded less dovish earlier today, adding hawkish friction to the carry regime while spot trades below the 160.00 watch level where intervention risks historically intensify. MOVE at 105.2 (96th percentile) vs VIX at 15.0 (11th percentile) reflects elevated bond market rate uncertainty that has not yet fed into broader equity volatility. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; structural carry demand runs directly into heavy options downside hedging. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — hold currently favored. Risk: A daily close above the SMA200 at 158.50 reopens upside momentum toward 160.00.

signals.title: NOK/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads G10 performance over 1W with an average gain of +0.778% across 2 pairs, while JPY lags at -0.353% across 7 pairs, establishing a 1.131% leader-to-laggard spread. Norges Bank policy rate sits at 4.5% in a hiking regime against BoJ at 1.25%, delivering a +325bp nominal policy differential in favor of the krone. Real policy rate differentials reinforce the divergence, with NOK printing at +1.82% restrictive vs JPY at -1.45% accommodative. Upward momentum in WTI crude to $90.10/bbl (+0.73% intraday) provides terms-of-trade support for NOK, while Japan's negative Economic Surprise Index (-10.6) contrasts with Norway's positive reading (+13.1). Trade bias: Bullish NOK/JPY, backed by bilateral momentum and a +325bp monetary spread. Catalyst: Japan Household Spending release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: WTI crude drops sharply below $85.00/bbl, unwinding the terms-of-trade driver.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Positioning + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1230, sitting below its SMA20 (1.1426), SMA50 (1.1524), and SMA200 (1.1608) daily cluster. Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a +135bp policy rate advantage for USD, reflected in an OIS SOFR-€STR spread of +145bp in USD's favor. Leveraged funds are net short EUR at -82,445 contracts (CFTC, week ending Sep 29), sitting at the 6th percentile of their 52-week distribution (z = -1.65) with WoW selling extending by -23,640 contracts. ATM implied volatility of 6.2% trades against realized HV30 of 3.9%, establishing an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.2% that demonstrates strong options demand for downside protection. The 20D US 5Y yield change (+54bp nominal, FRED as of Oct 2) was driven entirely by real yields (+54bp real, +0bp breakeven), sustaining fundamental dollar support despite retail positioning being 85% long EUR. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; monetary carry and real yield expansion reinforce the trend below moving average resistance. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes release at 18:00 UTC. Risk: Spot recovery and daily close above SMA20 at 1.1426, forcing leveraged short covering.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Carry Advantage Encounters Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6973, holding below its daily moving average cluster of SMA200 (0.7036), SMA20 (0.7065), and SMA50 (0.7093). The RBA policy rate of 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% creates a -60bp carry differential favoring AUD, mirrored in the OIS AONIA-SOFR basis of -71bp. Leveraged funds maintain net long positioning of +55,114 contracts (CFTC, week ending Sep 29), though net accumulation stalled WoW (-570 contracts) near the upper boundary of its historical band at the 79th percentile (z = +0.86). Australian 10Y sovereign yields trade at 5.41% (+10bp over US 10Y at 5.31%), but 1M 25d risk reversals at -0.94 confirm a persistent put skew that tempers bullish spot extensions. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; positive carry yield runs into solid technical resistance below 0.7036. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hold currently favored. Risk: A daily close above the SMA200 at 0.7036, which invalidates technical overhead pressure.
